scoring_justification: Recomputing the full Migdal-Eliashberg solver is computationally prohibitive in the verifier sandbox; we compare the agent's reported values against the paper's published Table I with tolerances and verify monotonic trends.

hidden_assets.purpose: Gold reference table from paper Table I for H3S at 9 pressures.
hidden_assets.source_provenance: Paper Table I (columns: P (GPa), Tc (K), δM (meV), αM (meV), δM-αM (meV)). Values taken verbatim.
hidden_assets.generation_method: Hardcoded from the published table in the paper (doi:10.48550/arXiv.2006.15248).
hidden_assets.why_not_fabricated: These are the actual published results; the reference solver also writes exactly these numbers.

outputs.description: Computed δM, αM, and δM−αM values for H3S at nine pressures. The checker compares each row against a hidden gold (paper’s Table I) with appropriate tolerances and verifies monotonic trends.

output_contract.notes: The CSV must contain exactly nine rows (one per pressure). The hidden checker will compare the reported numbers to the paper’s gold values using tolerances that account for implementation differences; it will also check that Tc decreases and δM−αM increases with pressure, as described in the paper.

steps.description: Verify CSV has exactly 9 rows, required columns, and no missing values.
Compare each row's Tc, dM, aM, dM_minus_aM against hidden gold with tolerances.
Verify Tc decreases with pressure and dM_minus_aM increases with pressure.
